confidence_notes: Medium overall. Restaurant and coffee anchors rest on several third-party aggregated sites (Expatistan, trek.zone, combien-coute.net, Intravel, city guides) with uneven and sometimes undated figures. Cocktail and wine are weaker: the cocktail is set near a single Expatistan club average (about EUR 11), and the wine glass is set from a retail bottle average (about EUR 9) adjusted to a restaurant glass. Both were cross-checked against the local beer relationship (cocktail about 2x beer, wine glass about 1.7x beer), so treat them as low-to-medium confidence. Beer is a 0.5 L domestic draught in a restaurant, anchored to about EUR 4.80 (Expatistan pub average), with tourist-core and Old Town prices likely higher. The three-course mid-range meal for two (no drinks) is a bounded estimate from mid-range per-person ranges of EUR 15-35, not a direct price. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge for July peak season; no accommodation search was run and no live listings or booking pages were inspected. The EUR-to-USD conversion (about 1.15) was assumed, not searched, so it adds uncertainty to every food and drink anchor. The FX observation (0.6947 USD per AUD, 2026-10-16) comes from a search-result summary of the RBA exchange rates page; the page itself was not opened directly.
comparable_city_reasoning: Tallinn is treated as a Baltic capital with restaurant and drink prices somewhat below Helsinki (per a koda.ee comparison) and in the mid-range of European mid-sized capitals. Numbeo's 2025 cost-of-living index places Tallinn 138th of 327 cities (score 52.7, New York City = 100), which supports this mid-to-lower European positioning. Accommodation is benchmarked to general July tourist-season rates for comparable Central and Northern European capitals, without a live check.
